pages.text: Personal storage is not merely a carried chest; it is a workbench that unfolds with cultivation. Its keybind can open over most non-text screens, and closing the terminal returns to the previous screen.

pages.title: Kongqiao and Xianqiao
pages.text: Stages one through five keep physical slots with expanded stack limits. At stage six, items become identity-based aggregates rather than a fixed grid. Stage seven adds fluids; stage eight adds FE, mana, source, chemicals and other external resources. The server stores every amount as a long value.

pages.title: Find, Store, Withdraw
pages.text: Search matches names, tooltips, tags and namespaces; sort by amount, name or mod. Scroll continuously and hold Shift for the authoritative amount. Buttons sort, deposit all, or withdraw the current filter. Typing E in search never closes the terminal.

pages.title: Fluids and External Resources
pages.text: Fluids use their animated material and display bucket amounts. Mekanism chemicals move through real containers; containerless resources such as FE use interfaces, crystals, AE2 or RS. Every transfer is server-validated, preserving remainders without 32-bit truncation.

pages.title: Craft in One Place
pages.text: Stage three opens a 3×3 crafting grid; stage four opens smithing. Missing ingredients refill from personal storage. JEI or EMI can transfer recipes when installed. Stage five adds the embedded Immortal Furnace, alongside equipment and fluid tabs.

pages.title: Magnet and Equipment
pages.text: The magnet sends drops within 13×13×13 directly into personal storage. Equipment uses vanilla inventory-slot semantics, so drag splitting and inventory sorters still understand it. Any remainder stays safe when storage cannot accept it.

pages.title: Realm Management
pages.text: After stage six, the management page shows owner, boundary and time scale. It switches noon/midnight and cycles clear, rain, thunder or snow. Settings affect only your realm; snow is a local particle presentation rather than server-wide precipitation.
